title: Quantization stability and SKU compatibility: A100 / H100 / L40S
content:
Objective:
Compare runtime stability (OOMs, silent corruption, crashes) and performance variance when running 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants of common serving models across A100 / H100 / L40S cloud SKUs and a small matrix of CUDA/driver versions. We want actionable guidance for:
- Which quantization formats to recommend per SKU (bnb 8-bit, GPTQ, FP16 fallback)
- Known driver/CUDA combos to avoid for production (reproducible instability)
- Runtime config tweaks that mitigate observed failures (jit flags, kernel fallbacks, allocator tuning)

Why this doc exists (context):
- Several customer incidents where dedicated pools running quantized models hit OOM/segfaults on H100 only.
- Internal reports of accuracy regressions after enabling auto-quantize pipeline on certain host types.
- Need to update Redwood Optimize suggestions and the model compatibility matrix.

Quick summary of findings (TL;DR):
- A100: most stable with bitsandbytes 0.41 + CUDA 11.8 driver 525.x; predictable memory use.
- H100: highest throughput for FP16 but shows sporadic allocator fragmentation with bnb 8-bit under CUDA 12.x + driver 535.x (we saw 2 distinct segfault patterns).
- L40S: behaves similar to A100 for quantized kernels but exhibits higher kernel launch latency for mixed-size sequences; batching spikes increase temporary memory pressure 
- Best short-term recommendation: pin serving pools that run quantized models to tested driver/CUDA combos and enable KV-cache pre-alloc linearization.

Experiment matrix (what we ran):
- Models: Llama-2-13B-chat (fp16 baseline), Llama-2-7B-q8 (bnb), custom 13B-GPTQ-4bit (GPTQ)
- SKUs: A100-80GB (nvidia cloud sku family), H100-80GB, L40S-48GB
- Driver / CUDA variants: driver 525.x / CUDA 11.8; driver 535.x / CUDA 12.1; driver 540.x / CUDA 12.2
- Serving runtime: Redwood inference runtime build 2024-09-18 + runtime flag set: continuous-batching enabled / kv-cache-prefetch off/on
- Quant libs: bitsandbytes 0.41, GPTQ fork (internal patch), torch 2.2 + torch-inductor / no-inductor runs for parity
- Workloads: short (seq=512) steady QPS, long (seq=4096) mixed QPS with random prefix lengths, and spike tests (microbursts)

Metrics collected:
- p50/p95/p99 token latencies (generation token step)
- throughput (tokens/sec) at sustained and burst QPS
- peak GPU memory usage and transient allocations (tracked via nvidia-smi sampling + runtime tracer)
- number of OOMs / segfaults / cuda-launch-failure logs
- output deviation (perplexity / deterministic token diffs) vs fp16 baseline

Detailed observations (raw-style notes):
1) H100 / CUDA12.x + bnb 8-bit:  
   - Observed two classes of failures: allocator fragmentation causing growing transient allocations until OOM after ~30–90 minutes under mixed-length workload; and immediate cuda-launch failures leading to segfaults when batch size scaled >4 for seq>=2048.  
   - Reproduced on two cloud SKUs with different firmware (so driver+cuda seems to be common factor).  
   - Workaround that helped in experiment: enable pre-allocated KV cache region (linearized allocation) and set environment BNB_NO_CUDA_KERNELS=1 (falls back to CPU kernels temporarily) — reduces crash frequency but increases tail latency.  

2) A100 / CUDA11.8 + bnb:  
   - Stable across long runs. Memory footprint expected; minor fragmentation observed but no growth loops. Throughput lower vs H100 for FP16 but quantized throughput comparable.  

3) L40S behavior:  
   - No segfaults but noticeable launch overheads for a lot of small kernels emitted by the GPTQ runtime; under bursty traffic p99 token latency spikes much higher compared to A100/H100.  
   - Memory headroom occasionally tighter than advertised for 48GB SKU because model + prefix KV + temporary kernels + cuBLAS workspace exceed aggressive fragmentation patterns.  

4) Accuracy and deterministic mismatch:  
   - GPTQ-4bit variants show larger token diffs vs fp16 baseline than bnb q8; however, the divergences are model+prompt dependent. Notably, under CUDA 12.2 we saw a subtle rounding mismatch in softmax kernels that changed top-token ordering for one eval prompt (JIRA: SRVINF-981).

5) Driver-specific kernel regressions:  
   - Driver 535.x had 2 open-source bug reports with similar stack traces (cudaXapi + malloc + cublasLt) — correlates with our segfaults on H100.  

Repro steps (so engineering can re-run quickly):
- Checkout runtime branch: refs/heads/quant-sku-stability-2024-10
- Deploy single-GPU instance on target SKU, install driver X (follow matrix), install bitsandbytes 0.41 + pytorch 2.2 wheel (linked in Confluence), set BNB_ALLOW_FALLBACK=1 for fallback testing.
- Run script: infra/bench/run_quant_stability.sh --model llama-2-13b --quant bnb --seq 4096 --qps 5 --duration 2h --log-level debug
- Collect runtime tracer: /var/log/redwood/traces/quant-stability/*.trace and attach GPU logs sampled at 1s via nvidia-smi

Data highlights (numbers excerpt):
- H100 (bnb 8-bit, CUDA12.1, driver 535.54): sustained throughput 1.8x A100 for fp16 baseline, but observed 3 segfaults in 2h run; p99 latency increased 3.2x during burst.
- A100 (bnb 8-bit, CUDA11.8, driver 525.105): throughput 1.0x baseline, 0 segfaults, stable memory curve.
- L40S (GPTQ-4bit, CUDA12.2): throughput similar to A100 for long sequences but p99 token latency spikes up to 6x under burst.

Actionable next steps (short-term):
- Pin dedicated pools running quantized models to A100 + CUDA11.8/driver-525.x until H100 driver issues are resolved.
- Add a runtime flag that pre-allocates KV cache and reserves a safety slab (config: kv-reserve-mib=1024) for quantized pools. Ship as beta in next runtime patch.
- Update Redwood Optimize suggestion: prefer bnb8 for production H100 only if driver+cuda pair validated; otherwise recommend fp16 or GPTQ with conservative batch limits.
- Create a Canary test that runs mixed-length workloads on H100 with quantized models every 6 hours; fail the canary if any segfault or OOM occurs.

Open questions / long-term research items:
- What changes in the cuBLAS/allocator interactions on H100+CUDA12 cause fragmentation loops under bnb kernels? Need to reproduce at micro-kernel level and open a driver bug with vendor.
- Evaluate whether compiler/kernel fusion (torch-inductor) contributes to the launch pattern that aggravates L40S. Could a different kernel scheduling reduce launch overhead?
- Explore a lightweight runtime allocator tuned for quantized kernels (reduce transient allocations, reuse workspace aggressively).

Appendix: quick config table we used (snapshot):
- runtime build: 2024-09-18+opt-kernel
- bnb: 0.41 (commit abc123 + internal patch to allocator)
- GPTQ: internal-gptq-v2
- torch: 2.2.0+inductor
- kernels: cuBLASLt (default)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add full TSV of traces to Confluence and attach sampling plots (peak mem over time, alloc count).
- Pair with firmware team to check for known H100 microcode updates.
- Draft short KB article for customer-success explaining recommended SKU-driver combos and short mitigation steps.

Unresolved: exact root cause for the H100 segfaults — we have a solid repro, but vendor confirmation required before recommending H100 for quantized workloads at scale.

(End of notes)
